result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, **Linear is the best project management tool if you're building a tech product**, while **Notion is the best all-rounder for an early-stage startup**\.

The right choice depends on your team size, how you work, and whether you need to manage software development, business operations, or both.

Here's how I'd compare the leading options.

## Best project management tools for startups

![Fast growing startups are built on Linear](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/piHpddRS6n9dTggcCRU3QzspXui7xfTg4qksC0xamyVTz0l5rmZLEYCGsVB7KKUouzfiOTbe-9ydzUq7UB2MFrNbZIGlaUSNjP0C8Bhd2CXnbxL2xZ05zw3USDTcATN8Ed4Fr3ygsGaA-sAB5VFRUeF1jd3BNolTylsoZGFQvpYkliFtHTL_AgaQh3gID9Z3?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product roadmaps and sprint planning.
- Clean, fast interface.
- Great for engineering and product teams.
- Integrates with GitHub and Slack.

**My take\:** Best if you're building a SaaS, app or technology product.

[Linear website](https://linear.app/)

---

![Project Management Notion Template for Teams](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/Bglcmq1EQK9asvjwbKlF1Ik04e4pVno80aG8dCSB-rJBqMq393egud3X0Iy9yQCeqdQoqkGH143RsgaiSXAumfORHv0z1HQCPOBfSbxsib_oIgPNQhrl2QWYnpUU2pzM0asP9NTUKqJtJlroPExSIdw-ytyzORKO-GOVlnE-kmZ0OzdvB_lssnIglNOcWHRO?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Notion**

(Best for early-stage startups)

- Project management and documentation together.
- Company wiki, meeting notes and SOPs.
- Customisable task databases.
- Useful for keeping company knowledge organised.

**My take\:** Excellent for founders who want one central company workspace.

[Notion website](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![Finastra Customer Story | ClickUp™](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OXxUksa73j7hoTxbYQ6zo3pspX36GflPBLMsRWXjhfWZTJdFq6md_tXaxCCc_3Kjh0xQSrUSgXoCYi3d5TOe48r-mvzFwLplQbgf4lhsH3q_bsATt_hAcyva5qI1DtZG8OasgRxxldReZAIfURcJdNdt2Br8nPVvqn-lCO5aR2MxpFl9QAiCxibf4gzehOOb?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. ClickUp**

(Best all-in-one solution)

- Tasks, projects, docs and goals.
- Dashboards and reporting.
- Automations and multiple project views.
- Highly configurable.

**My take\:** Probably the strongest choice if you want to manage the entire startup in one platform.

[ClickUp website](https://clickup.com/)

---

![Dashboard UI Best Practices for Insightful Data Visualization](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/-WmCS1rnvdMdE6Qau-Q7buM9ydD8Cjx07J6sQsqPM8mU3Wee6ZkUpRxZ9O3SXqFdl8F_lwdUkmbOyujI6Pju7u9hpyknrVsX05U-NSSEGKEH-HDxsLh4uwzptn8rXnHsLXEwiayRQu4-R7-vCZXvKAEC0X7RrmzhXlDFP9tOAwb5VNhC9K2elmeo3dKcRv_9?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Clear task ownership and accountability.
- Project timelines and dependencies.
- Good cross-team coordination.
- Useful management reporting.

**My take\:** Great when you have multiple departments and need everyone aligned.

[Asana website](https://asana.com/)

---

![Portfolio management - All Projects Dashboard – Support](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/-5NH-hROEcQXpSQPmMUJv0x7GODAoqXeNRlBaAmeb5yjL6ws1fsUSsHXZKs7cGHwGwKjC6qsKZvaA0-fO7oD8-9_bc-PbX0_EJ1QpOPifoMbrdCVNNuollQzaJIhYGySdgXpxRYlPlDaiOA8sl0RXCUZIj48mjl4S_hb7oB4Rygmeul72nI4kZxZvS769XKO?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

- Highly visual project dashboards.
- Sales, marketing and operational workflows.
- Automation and reporting.
- Easy for non-technical teams.

**My take\:** Particularly good for startups with lots of operational projects.

[Monday.com website](https://monday.com/)

These choices are consistent with recent 2026 startup software comparisons, although individual rankings vary depending on the team's needs. ## My comparison

| Tool | Best use | Complexity |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Linear | Product development | Low |
| Notion | Company-wide workspace | Low–medium |
| ClickUp | Everything in one place | Medium–high |
| Asana | Team accountability | Medium |
| Monday.com | Business operations | Medium |


## What I'd actually recommend

For a startup with a small team (2–15 people), I'd shortlist these two approaches\:

**Option A: Lean startup**

- Notion for documentation, company knowledge and planning.
- Linear for product development.
- Slack for communication.

**Option B: All-in-one startup**

- ClickUp for tasks, projects, goals and documentation.
- Slack for communication.

I'd lean towards Option A for a technology startup and Option B for a startup with lots of different business functions.

## A few questions to narrow it down

I can make a much more precise recommendation if I know a little about the startup.

**1\. What type of startup is it?**

---

**2\. How big is the team?**

---

**3\. What stage are you at?**

---

**4\. What do you primarily want to manage?**

[Get my recommendation]

I'll use those answers to recommend the best tool, rather than just the most feature-rich one.
